statement.excerpt: At $1.25 trillion (as mentioned above), OpenAI would need a much better listing price than Anthropic is expected to have, for a company with objectively worse metrics, including slower growth, lower revenue, higher costs, and hundreds of millions of free users that generate, at best, about a billion dollars in “annualized” ad revenue against the billions of dollars it costs to serve their compute.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a comparison of financial performance on comparable definitions, rather than a comparison of differently defined headline figures.
Use July–September 2026, the latest completed quarter before publication. Compare revenue growth over the same interval and costs covering the same activities.

The advertising figure is explicitly annualized. It must be compared with an annualized serving-cost estimate for the same free-user population, not with an unrelated quarterly expense or total company spending.
The financial comparison draws on press estimates in the surrounding text. The advertising announcement separately uses company-reported figures.
The single metric_scope summarizes several components; their realized and annualized measures must remain separate.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish lower OpenAI revenue and revenue growth, higher comparable costs, hundreds of millions of free users, and roughly $1 billion or less in annualized free-user advertising revenue against several billion dollars in comparable annual serving costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish the reverse of a stated financial comparison or show that free-user advertising revenue was materially above the stated ceiling or covered comparable serving costs. Conflicting components would warrant mixed rather than a blanket verdict.
